answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before it can vote, with one vote per bond. Agents such as quartz, kernel, and lantern each face the same rule. Creating aliases gives an attacker no free voting power: controlling 1,000 votes requires locking 1,000 bonds. The defense makes influence proportional to committed capital, imposing financing costs even if the attacker later recovers every bond.
